note.text: Because, given that and since can introduce premises; therefore, thus and so can introduce conclusions. These are clues, not guarantees. Since can mark elapsed time; so can intensify a description. Arguments may omit indicators entirely. Identify what is offered as support and what is meant to follow. Changing an indicator without checking its role can reverse the argument.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to interpret indicator expressions by their role in context rather than spotting words mechanically. Builds on: argument parts and complete claims. Leads to: opposition and reconstruction of reasoning.

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original examples: The venue needs checking because it remains provisional. Here because introduces a reason. The venue remains provisional; therefore the notice should not call it confirmed. Here therefore introduces a conclusion. Bih has waited since Monday uses since temporally, not as a premise indicator.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Read the whole passage. Replace an apparent premise cue with given that and test the relation; replace a conclusion cue with it follows that. Treat those substitutions as meaning checks rather than automatic proofs of validity.

Therefore the notice needs correction introduces the target.
Since Monday marks time, not an offered reason.
The room is provisional. Calling it confirmed misleads readers.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve scope, terms and assumptions.
example: Because always introduces the conclusion being supported. Correction: In this argumentative use it introduces the reason.
Therefore proves an argument valid by its spelling. Correction: An indicator marks intention rather than guaranteeing support.
Since always signals a premise whatever its use. Correction: The temporal phrase is a counterexample.
A passage without therefore can never contain reasoning. Correction: A support relation can be conveyed without an indicator.

pick.q: Correct the notice because the venue is provisional. What follows because?
e: No time phrase follows it.
Correction is the supported proposal.
An indicator guarantees no truth.

pick.q: The venue is provisional; thus the notice needs checking. What follows thus?
e: The reason precedes thus.
Thus does not name a starting day.
A complete claim follows it.
pick.y: The checking claim is meant to follow.

pick.q: Bih has waited since Monday. What does since do?
e: The phrase supplies time, not an offered reason.
There is no supported conclusion here.
Since is not a negation.

pick.q: All voters have badges. Bih votes. Bih has a badge. No indicator appears. Which assessment is accurate?
pick.r: The final claim can still be presented as following from the earlier claims.
w: No reasoning is possible without therefore.
Every sentence is an isolated question.
The last claim must be a premise solely because it is last.
e: Indicators are optional clues.
These are assertions.
Position alone does not identify a role.
